A 16-bit SNES-style PIXEL ART character ATTACK sheet on a SOLID FLAT PURE WHITE background (#FFFFFF, completely uniform). Layout: 3 ROWS by 3 COLUMNS of sprites, evenly spaced, with a wide empty white margin on all four sides and a clear white gap between every sprite — nothing may touch, overlap or be cut off by any edge, especially the bottom row. Every sprite is the SAME character at the SAME size and the SAME pixel scale. THE CHARACTER, drawn identically in all nine frames: {CHARACTER}. THE THREE COLUMNS are ONE SWING of the weapon, left to right. It is a SLASH — an arcing sweep across the body — NOT a stab, NOT a thrust, NOT the weapon pointed straight ahead like a spear (asking for 'an attack' produces a stab by default, which is wrong for a bladed weapon): Column 1 = WIND-UP, the weapon pulled back and raised on one side, arm cocked, body coiled, blade angled away from the target before any contact. Column 2 = STRIKE, mid-slash — the weapon sweeping through an ARC across the front of the body at the moment it connects, blade angled across the direction of travel rather than pointing along it, arm extended through the swing; the biggest, clearest pose of the three. Column 3 = RECOVER, the follow-through — the weapon carried past the target and down on the far side of the arc, body settling back. THE THREE ROWS are directions, and the direction must hold across ALL THREE frames of its row without exception: Row 1 = seen from the FRONT, facing the viewer, attacking toward the viewer. Row 2 = strict SIDE PROFILE FACING RIGHT — head in profile, nose pointing right, one shoulder to the viewer, in all three frames including the wind-up and the recovery; never turned to face the viewer. Row 3 = seen from BEHIND — the back of the head and body, NO face, NO eyes, attacking away from the viewer. ART STYLE: chunky flat cartoon pixel art, big simple shapes, flat solid colours, a thick black outline, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering, no texture inside a colour block. Nothing else in the image: no grid lines, no boxes, no frames, no labels, no text, no numbers, no shadows.
